title: SafelyYou Guardian real-time AI video fall alerts cut residents' time on the ground by about 30 minutes in six California memory care facilities
summary: In six California memory care facilities, real-time alerts from SafelyYou Guardian's AI video fall detection cut residents' time on the ground after a fall by 29.6 minutes.
account: SafelyYou Guardian combines continuous video monitoring with computer vision algorithms that detect falls and notify caregivers. Researchers from SafelyYou, three University of California campuses (San Francisco, Davis and Berkeley), MIT and Sorbonne Université installed it in the bedrooms of consenting residents in six California memory care facilities from November 2017 to August 2018. Staff received no regular video review in a baseline period (November to December 2017), weekly video review from January to April 2018, and real-time notification of falls from May to August 2018. The study recorded 436 falls among 66 residents with Alzheimer disease or related dementias, and fallers could not stand up alone in 97.6% of cases. Between the baseline and real-time periods, time until staff assistance fell by 28.3 minutes and time on the ground fell by 29.6 minutes (95% CI 20.3 to 38.9). The share of fallers who lay on the ground for more than an hour fell from 31% (8 of 26) to none. The Journal of Medical Internet Research published the study on 17 June 2021. The design is a before and after comparison without a concurrent control group. Every author was a current or former SafelyYou employee, board member, adviser or shareholder. A 2023 systematic review by Imperial College London authors, who declare no conflicts of interest, lists the same reductions and judges that the system improves care after falls.
